content.text: Goal: project success. This is mainly defined as getting by today 18:00 local time (berlin) approval from Jörn that the thesis writeup is of PASSing grade/quality. There's one parallel agent running in a herdr pane, named "datascience | msc-math" iiuc. It is working on a bunch of stuff, you'll need to coordinate with it, but iiuc it's mostly doing datascience and so there's no strong overlap with finding a good writing workflow, cleaning up the repo, replacing expensive and slow full-text reviews from Jörn with cheaper review feedback loops (e.g. moving work Jörn does to codex, once we know how to do it with codex / with less involvement from Jörn). My guess is to establish ground truths for that, e.g. a dataset of (text, review) pairs that Jörn does on his own, and then to see whether codex can replace the text=>review function or at least speed it up in some way (e.g. it makes little sense to let Jörn spend 5m to type up all the layout issues, when a luna agent can take a screenshot + read the latex + use visual reasoning + flag all issues in 60s). Similarly it's plausible that astra, but not sol, is now good enough at predicting mathematical community's research taste, that asking Jörn for evaluation is no longer quite as valuable per minute as it was relative to what sol could provide. I think you should first ask the existing agent for a report, familiarize yourself (luna explorers) with the repo + project, interrogate me about all you are not confident enough about to proceed without my feedback. Then check in with me by describing the is-state, the target-state, the division of ocncerns with the datascience agent, and what the biggest / most urgent unknowns are right now -- and whether you already know how to resolve them cheaply/efficeintly. Probably this also involves listing the rules/constraints you want to operate under -- as a way to ensure you don't commit some mistake classes / that you recover from them. Questions? Clarification requests? Pushback?

> We have about 2¼ hours until 18:00 Berlin. How much reading/review time can you make available before then, and is there a latest time you need the final candidate? This determines how much time we can spend on calibration versus writing.

about 2h15min of reading time can be made available! if this target deadline is not realistic ,i can change m y plans -- please tell me so early however

Your availability helps substantially. I can’t yet responsibly forecast approval by 18:00: the current 110-page manuscript is judged failing, and its replacement is still at sample and partial-chapter stage. That is a concrete risk to the deadline, even with nearly all your remaining time available for reading. If changing your plans requires advance notice, preserve that option now. I’m finishing the ownership and completeness check so I can give you a better-grounded assessment shortly.

Your sample feedback gives us the first useful calibration result: the prose is comfortable and of passing quality, but the narrative lacks structure. My frozen review anticipated some placement issues, but missed the main need to organize the chapter around discovering patterns and turning them back into mathematical conjectures. That is a material miss. The data-science agent is restructuring the chapter around your stated approach.

I’m also updating the shared work map to reflect the new feedback. The main uncertainty is now clearer: a structurally revised chapter can still fail at sentence level. Agent review has not yet shown that it reliably catches your objections.
small side: rn i have no pending async task with a review request
Thanks—I had incorrectly treated the earlier HKO request as still pending. I’m resubmitting it now.

The server now records a successful HKO PDF download, so the delivery problem appears resolved. It’s 16:30 Berlin: about 90 minutes remain. The whole candidate is around 80 pages, including appendices and references; whether that leaves enough time for your PASS judgment remains uncertain, especially if HKO needs substantial revision.

While you read HKO, I’ll record a short prediction of where its explanation may become difficult. Comparing that with your actual feedback will give us another concrete test of whether agent review can save you time.

The HKO prediction is recorded before your feedback, so I won’t revise it to fit your response. I’m leaving that PDF unchanged and checking the latest introduction’s pagination in the assembled draft.

The preflight of the preliminaries and generalized-characteristic proof found no material followability issue in that scope. I’ll leave those sections unchanged for now and continue folding in your introduction feedback.

"1.3 Looking for mathematical structure in data" again a bit too detailed i think for the introduction chapter. 1.4. is lacking a bit of motivation -- why this order, what to read vs skip etc. ;; overall i think the literature review is plainly missing??? i'd have epxected basic references here such as "c_EHZ = c_zylindrical for symplectically convex bodies, which cinlcudes convex bodies" (a somewhat recent result iirc?)

The HKO paper explicitly lists \(c_{\mathrm{EHZ}}=c_Z\) for convex domains in \(\mathbb R^4\) as open (Remark 1.4(v)). Edtmair’s nearby result identifies cylindrical capacity with a minimum surface-of-section area; equality of all normalized capacities is proved near the ball. I’ll distinguish these in the literature review. [HKO paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16513), [Edtmair](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00039-024-00689-4).

The literature addition passed its source-scope check after two small hypothesis corrections. I’m preparing the revised candidate. With about half an hour left, whole-thesis approval by 18:00 is still uncertain; the missing literature context was a substantive gap, not just a wording fix.

> Continue the whole-thesis PASS review with the revised 86-page PDF: http://100.70.188.20:57101/CZPvy_O6JPwfoeARRCp1f326-0.pdf . Preliminaries start on page 7. No immediate rereading of the introduction or HKO is requested; read where you need evidence for your overall judgment. Please report the next material obstacle, or whole-thesis PASS if you have enough evidence. Fallback file: /workspaces/msc-math/.git/codex/thesis-review-1730/main.pdf.

"The later computations replace a boundary-dynamics problem by finite data from the facets of
a polytope." sloppy written - are you sure this chapter is ready to read/review by me? this feels like sth codex (astra) ought to be able to flag if asked to pay attention to thsi class of mistake / the wider open class of writing quality issues?

No—I overstated its readiness. The preflight checked mathematical prerequisites and inference gaps, not prose quality at the standard your annotations establish. That was the wrong check to use before sending you onward.

Please pause the preliminaries review. I’ll review the prose before asking you to spend more reading time on it.

I’m using the process-correction skill to change the review itself. The new pass will read sentence by sentence for clarity and purpose, with your annotations as examples—not as an exhaustive checklist. Mathematical correctness will be reported separately from writing readiness.

prelim: i will now skip this chapter given the rate of errors, and move to 4) the quadratic program -- bc maybe it reveals new error types that need to b e reviewed-for / addressed; since here writing agents may mix up how to write for computer scientists vs hwo to write for matehmaticians

The preliminaries failure changes my deadline assessment: at this correction rate, I no longer consider whole-thesis approval by 18:00 realistic. If your evening plans depend on it, please plan for the target to slip. I’ll continue the repairs, but I can’t yet give a reliable replacement time.
